questions.title: Clopper-Pearson exact binomial confidence interval
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Clopper and Pearson (1934). Let X be Binomial(n,p), observe X=x, and write alpha=1-confidence_level for a two-sided equal-tailed interval. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, derive the lower endpoint by inverting the upper binomial tail and the upper endpoint by inverting the lower binomial tail. Establish the equivalent beta-quantile formulas, including lower=0 when x=0 and upper=1 when x=n. Prove that the resulting random interval has coverage at least 1-alpha for every p in [0,1], and explain why discreteness generally makes coverage conservative rather than exactly nominal. Establish interval ordering, containment in [0,1], complement symmetry under x -> n-x, and nesting as confidence_level increases. Distinguish the construction from Wilson, Wald, mid-p, and Bayesian equal-tailed intervals, and do not use simulation as proof. The required model-authored artifact is est_clopper_pearson_interval and must implement the frozen Python run_estimator(request) contract exactly. Exploratory Python or R may diagnose endpoint identities and boundary cases. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses predeclared n, p, and confidence settings, independently enumerates exact coverage over all binomial counts, and compares repeated-sampling coverage with that exact value using Monte Carlo uncertainty. This is implementation and calibration evidence, not proof of the universal coverage statement. Source-code replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

primary_paper.title: The Use of Confidence or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial

implementation_convention.title: SciPy BinomTestResult.proportion_ci exact method
implementation_convention.meaning: The exact method denotes the two-sided Clopper-Pearson interval; the task contract below is the executable authority.

request_fields.name: successes
request_fields.meaning: The observed exact integer success count x.
request_fields.indexing: the observed binomial count for this request
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, floats, strings, negative values, and values exceeding trials; do not coerce.

request_fields.name: trials
request_fields.meaning: The exact positive integer binomial trial count n.
request_fields.indexing: the binomial sample size for this request
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, floats, strings, zero, and negative values; do not coerce.

request_fields.name: confidence_level
request_fields.shape: one finite scalar strictly between zero and one
request_fields.indexing: one confidence level for the request
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonfinite values, zero, one, and values outside (0,1); do not coerce.

response_fields.name: estimate
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals zero at successes=0 and one at successes=trials.

response_fields.name: lower
response_fields.edge_cases: Exactly zero when successes is zero; otherwise the alpha/2 quantile of Beta(successes,trials-successes+1).

response_fields.name: upper
response_fields.edge_cases: Exactly one when successes equals trials; otherwise the 1-alpha/2 quantile of Beta(successes+1,trials-successes).

response_fields.name: width
response_fields.meaning: The interval width under the declared endpoint convention.
response_fields.shape: one finite nonnegative scalar at most one
response_fields.edge_cases: Must equal upper-lower without clipping or alternate interval substitution.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly successes, trials, and confidence_level, and the response contains exactly estimate, lower, upper, and width. Missing, extra, malformed, nonfinite, or coercible-only values are rejected.
For every admitted request, 0<=lower<=estimate<=upper<=1 and width=upper-lower; lower is exactly zero at x=0 and upper exactly one at x=n.
For the same trials and confidence level, replacing successes x by n-x maps [lower,upper] to [1-upper,1-lower], maps estimate to 1-estimate, and preserves width.
For fixed successes and trials, increasing confidence_level cannot increase lower or decrease upper, so interval width cannot decrease.

empirical_claims.meaning: Every frozen scenario fixes trials, true p, confidence_level, seed, replicate count, and thresholds before outcomes and invokes the accepted estimator through the exact public request.
For every possible count in each frozen scenario, returned endpoints match an independent beta-quantile implementation and satisfy the declared complement, nesting, ordering, and boundary identities.
Summing Binomial(trials,p) probabilities over exactly those counts whose returned interval contains p gives frozen-scenario coverage at least confidence_level.

Repeated Binomial(trials,p) sampling produces coverage compatible with the independently enumerated candidate coverage under a predeclared Monte Carlo standard-error rule; this does not prove universal coverage.
